subject: Urgent: Unexpected 429 burst and retry storm during peak ingestion
messages:
From: ops+alerts@healthhaven.com
To: rohan_mehta@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: helen.park@healthhaven.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Realtime: spike in 429s + timeouts across ingestion endpoints

Hi team,

We started seeing a sudden spike in 429 responses and a corresponding retry amplification across our ingestion tier starting ~08:45 PDT. Throughput dropped and multiple pipelines timed out. Attached is a short log excerpt showing repeated client retries and 429s (healthhaven_request_log_excerpt.txt).

Key impact:
- 429 rate climbed from ~0.5% to ~22% in 25 minutes
- Several downstream consumers hit 5xx timeouts after retry storms
- SLA alerts triggered for transaction latency and throughput loss

Can you confirm whether this is a configuration change on Redwood's side (quota/tiering) or an upstream backpressure issue? We need an ETA for mitigation — currently this is a production P1 for us.

Sandeep Reddy
Head of Platform Ops, HealthHaven
ops+alerts@healthhaven.com
From: rohan_mehta@redwood.ai
To: ops+alerts@healthhaven.com, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime: spike in 429s + timeouts across ingestion endpoints

Thanks Sandeep — we see the alert and are triaging immediately.

Short plan (first 30m):
- Triage scope: confirm whether HealthHaven's org/project mapping was recently changed during the cutover window.
- Check rate-limiter assignments and tiering decisions (service telemetry).
- Apply temporary lift on project quota where safe and enable fallback routing to the dedicated pool if capacity is available.
- Ask HealthHaven to enable exponential backoff + jitter on client side for the next hour to dampen retry amplification.

Marissa — can you run the quota-mapping query and surface the project->org tier mapping? Sean/Karthik, please stand by for quick rollback or temp patch. I'll update Ops in 10–15 minutes.

—Rohan
Rohan Mehta
Sr. Customer Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: rohan_mehta@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:31:42 -07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime: spike in 429s + timeouts across ingestion endpoints

Quick findings:
- I queried the tier-assignment service and found HealthHaven's primary project (proj-hh-ingest) is *incorrectly* flagged as TIER-LOW (quota 2k rps) instead of TIER-PROD (15k rps). This appears to be an aliasing bug introduced by last night's label normalization job (label rewrite rule #LH-9).
- Rate-limiter metrics show a sudden surge of client retries beginning 08:45; retry window traffic shows clients retrying at fixed 1s intervals (no jitter) which amplified the enforced 429s into a retry storm.
- We have spare capacity in the dedicated pool in us-west-2 for the next 3 hours.

Recommended immediate actions (I can do these now with a config push):
1) Flip proj-hh-ingest to TIER-PROD (temporary override)
2) Increase per-project burst window to accommodate current backlog ( +20% for 1 hour)
3) Enable routing of HealthHaven traffic to the dedicated pool (fail-open to that pool)

I attached a short trace image showing the retry amplification (retry-storm-trace.png) and a JSON blob with the proposed temp quota change (proposed-temp-quota-change.json).

If we push 1–3 now we should see 429s drop below 1.5% within ~8–12 minutes and throughput restore.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Success — Escalations, Redwood Inference
From: rohan_mehta@redwood.ai
To: ops+alerts@healthhaven.com, helen.park@healthhaven.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, leadership@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:45:30 -07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime: spike in 429s + timeouts across ingestion endpoints

Sandeep / Helen — immediate update and remediation plan:

What we found: label normalization introduced an alias that caused your primary ingest project to be assigned to a lower quota tier. That, combined with client retries at fixed short intervals, produced an amplified wave of 429s.

What we are doing now (in flight):
- Temporary override applied: proj-hh-ingest -> TIER-PROD; burst window increased; routing enabled to dedicated us-west-2 pool.
- Advising HealthHaven to enable exponential backoff + jitter on retries (please apply this change ASAP).
- We will monitor 429 rate and latency metrics and keep you updated every 10 minutes.

Compensations/exec note: our support team will apply a one-time service credit for the impacted hour while we stabilize. I'll follow up with the account team to coordinate formal credit paperwork.

ETA: expect visible improvement 10–15 minutes after the override; I'll confirm when 429s fall back to baseline.

—Rohan Mehta
Sr. Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: rohan_mehta@redwood.ai
To: leadership@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-incident summary & executive action items — HealthHaven 429 burst (June 14)

Team — final summary for execs and next steps:

Timeline recap:
- 08:45 PDT: HealthHaven client traffic spikes; 429 rate climbs to ~22% due to tier misassignment + client retry patterns.
- 09:31 PDT: Triage discovers aliasing bug in label normalization; project assigned to TIER-LOW.
- 09:45 PDT: Temporary override and routing to dedicated pool applied; client jitter rolled out at 09:52; 429s returned to baseline (~0.8%) by ~10:05.

Root cause: label normalization rule LH-9 created a label alias that misrouted proj-hh-ingest to the wrong quota tier. Secondary factor: clients issuing tight fixed-interval retries with no jitter caused amplification.

Immediate mitigations completed:
- Temporary tier override + burst increase, routing switch to dedicated pool
- Customer requested to apply jitter/backoff (applied)
- One-time credit offered to customer for impacted window (account team to formalize)

Permanent remediation plan (owners and timeline):
- Fix label normalization to prevent aliasing (Infra: Karthik, ETA 2027-06-18)
- Add canary checks for tier assignment post-deploy (SRE: Sean, ETA 2027-06-21)
- Implement automatic detection for retry amplification patterns and alerting (Platform: Marissa, ETA 2027-06-30)
- Add a safety override path for critical customers to fail-open to dedicated pools (Product/SRE, ETA 2027-07-05)

Please review and let me know if execs want a short readout for HealthHaven leadership. I'll attach the full postmortem doc and the incident dashboards to the support ticket.

—Rohan Mehta
Sr. Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
